q: Sound is a sequence of ____ waves which propagates through compressible media such as air or water.
e: Sound is a sequence of pressure waves in a compressible medium such as air or water. It is longitudinal, not a transverse electromagnetic wave. Vacuum has nothing to compress, so sound stops there.

q: During their propagation, waves can be reflected, ____ or attenuated by the medium.
e: Refraction bends a wave when its speed changes from one medium to another. Sound can be reflected, refracted or attenuated as it travels. Attenuation is the weakening; refraction is the bend.

q: During their propagation, waves can be reflected, refracted or ____ by the medium.
e: While sound travels it can be reflected, refracted or attenuated by the medium. Polarization is not the usual sound story in this chapter. Attenuation is the weakening, not amplification.

q: A relationship between density and pressure, affected by ____, determines the speed of sound within the medium.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Stiffer media generally carry it faster.

q: The ____ of the medium determines the rate at which sound is attenuated.
e: Attenuation is the weakening of a wave as it travels, often by viscosity. Air and water usually damp sound only a little this way. Amplification would require an extra energy source.

q: For many media, such as air or water, attenuation due to ____ is negligible.
e: Attenuation is loss of wave amplitude along the path. Viscosity sets that damping rate for sound. In many everyday media the viscous loss is small.

q: Speed of a sound wave can also be affected by the density, temperature, and ____ of the medium through which the sound waves travel.
e: Sound speed depends on density, temperature and elasticity of the medium. Different media therefore have different speeds. Frequency and amplitude are not the speed-setters here.

q: In a solid medium, the speed of sound depends on Young's modulus and the ____ of the solid material.
e: In a solid, v = sqrt(Y/rho), Young's modulus over density. Y and the bulk modulus are elasticity properties, unit N m^-2. Liquids use bulk modulus B instead of Y.

q: In liquids, the velocity of sound depends on the ____ modulus and density of liquid.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Stiffer media generally carry it faster. Liquids the velocity of sound depends on cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: In gases, the velocity of sound depends on the ____ constant of gas, pressure in gas and its density.
e: Adiabatic means Q = 0, no heat in or out, often by insulating the system. First law collapses to Delta U = -W. Gamma = Cp/Cv then appears in the reversible adiabatic relations.

q: Longitudinal sound waves travel faster in ____ than they do in liquids than they do in gases.

q: The level of intensity of a sound is measured relative to a reference intensity value $I_0$, taken as ____ which correspond to the minimum intensity of sound that can be heard.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself.

q: The minimum intensity of sound that can be heard is also known as the threshold of ____ or minimum audible intensity.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself. A minimum is destructive interference.

q: The ____ (dB) is the unit used for measuring sound intensity (intensity level of sound).
e: The decibel measures sound intensity level, 10 log10(I/I_0). Each extra 10 dB is about ten times the loudness. Hertz is frequency; watt is power; dB is this logarithmic level.

q: For every 10 dB added to the sound level, the loudness of the sound is increased by ____ times.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective.

q: A 120 dB sound will be ____ times louder than a 100 dB sound.
e: A 20 dB jump is two factors of 10, so 120 dB is about 100 times louder than 100 dB. Ten times would have been only 10 dB. The scale is logarithmic in intensity.

q: Sound intensity is a direct measure of the ____ reaching an eardrum measured in $W m^{-2}$.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area at the eardrum, in W m^-2. The dB number is the level of that intensity, not the intensity unit itself. Force or energy without time and area are the wrong measures.

q: The intensity level of sound at the threshold of hearing is ____ dB.
e: Threshold of hearing is the minimum audible intensity, I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2, which is 0 dB. It is a minimum, not a maximum or a pain limit. Levels in decibels compare I to that I_0.
